ledger.x: c. 3150 BC: Upper and Lower Egypt are united and the Early Dynastic Period begins. Page: 'the era of ancient Egypt that immediately follows the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt in c. 3150 BC'; it describes the unification as a gradual process over perhaps a few centuries (a paraphrase, no date). The page names the…
With the First Dynasty the capital moves from Thinis to Memphis: 'With the First Dynasty, the Egyptian capital moved from Thinis to Memphis.'

c. 2686 BC: the Early Dynastic Period gives way to the Old Kingdom. Page: the period lasts 'until c. 2686 BC, or the beginning of the Old Kingdom'; the Old Kingdom page reads 'Began: c. 2686 BC' and Djoser (Third Dynasty) as its first king.

wars.name: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt
wars.outcome: The page mentions 'a campaign to conquer Lower Egypt and the Nile Delta' (Narmer/Menes) and dates the unification to c.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the state is the Nile valley and Delta, bounded by desert and by Elephantine in the south.
